issue.title: sase bead doctor reports 14 settled historical event-stream rewrites as permanent ERRORs
issue.description:
Discovered 2026-08-16 after repairing the bead-store wedge.

'sase bead doctor' on a healthy, fully-synced store prints 14 ERROR lines for event-stream rewrites that are already settled history, e.g.:

  ERROR: bead event stream sase-m5 rewrote event 3; first offending commit a2c29f164c6a
  ERROR: bead event stream sase-j7 is shorter than its own history: missing events 62-63 present in ancestor 7e3d27461b3a
  ERROR: bead event stream sase-mk rewrote event 2; first offending commit 4dfa41f5ad5d

These are backward-looking. The guard already settled each one at the time by restoring ancestor bytes, and the store commits and pushes cleanly now: verified by three real mutations (close sase-m9.3.1.5, close sase-mi.6, and the 8-agent epic graph commit for sase-mq) all committing and pushing without incident, and by mutating one bead in a full 853-stream scratch copy and confirming every other stream stayed byte-identical.

The problem is signal quality, not correctness. A doctor that always prints 14 ERRORs on a healthy store trains agents and the owner to ignore its ERROR section, so a genuinely new rewrite will not stand out. That directly cost time during this incident: distinguishing the one live, blocking rewrite from the 14 dead ones required manual event-by-event comparison.

Scope: give settled historical rewrites a distinct, non-ERROR classification (baseline/acknowledged/settled) so ERROR is reserved for rewrites that are currently blocking, and keep the historical set inspectable on demand. Deliberately excludes any history rewrite of the bead store; the committed events stay as they are.
